Rashi on Berakhot 51a:11:2.english: In [the case of asparagus made] of wine - One should not spit.

Rashi on Berakhot 51a:11:3.hebrew: בדשכרא - אם לא רק מים הבאים בפיו אחריו, לוקה:
Rashi on Berakhot 51a:11:3.english: With [asparagus of] beer - If he did not spit out the water that comes into his mouth after [drinking] it, he is stricken [with illness].

Rashi on Berakhot 51a:12:1.english: Even before the king - He should spit and not endanger himself.

Rashi on Berakhot 51a:13:1.english: Suriel - An important angel [privileged] to come before the Holy One, Blessed be He.

Rashi on Berakhot 51a:13:2.hebrew: אל תטול חלוקך - שחרית מיד השמש, אלא אתה בעצמך טלהו ממקום שהוא שם ותלבשנו:
Rashi on Berakhot 51a:13:2.english: Do not take your cloak - In the morning from the hand of the attendant; rather, you yourself take it from the place where it is and put it on.

Rashi on Berakhot 51a:13:3.english: Takhsefit - The name of a band of demons.

Rashi on Berakhot 51a:13:4.english: Istalganit - The name of a band of angels of destruction.

Rashi on Berakhot 51a:13:5.hebrew: אימתי יבא אדם לידי אחד מן הדברים הללו וילכד - רבי ישמעאל עלה לרקיע על ידי שם, בברייתא דמעשה מרכבה:
Rashi on Berakhot 51a:13:5.english: When will a person come to one of these things and be trapped - Rabbi Yishmael ascended to the firmament by means of a [Divine] Name, [as recounted] in the Baraita of Ma'aseh Merkavah.

Rashi on Berakhot 51a:16:1.english: A cup of blessing - [The cup of] Grace after Meals.

Rashi on Berakhot 51a:16:2.hebrew: הדחה ושטיפה וכו' - כולהו מפרש להו ואזיל:
Rashi on Berakhot 51a:16:2.english: Rinsing and washing, etc. - [The Gemara] proceeds to explain all of them.

Rashi on Berakhot 51a:16:3.hebrew: מן הקרקע - אם ע"ג קרקע הסב, ואם על גבי שלחן — מגביהו מן השלחן:
Rashi on Berakhot 51a:16:3.english: From the ground - [This applies] if he reclined on the ground; but if [he reclined] at a table, he lifts it from the table.

Rashi on Berakhot 51a:16:4.english: As a gift - By way of a gift and esteem.

Rashi on Berakhot 51a:16:5.english: To members of his household - To his wife.

Rashi on Berakhot 51a:17:1.hebrew: חי - שמוזגו במים לאחר שנתנו בכוס חי. אבל לברך עליו חי — הא אמרן במתני' אין מברכין. אי נמי: חי בלע"ז פריש"ק — להביאו מן החבית לשמו:
Rashi on Berakhot 51a:17:1.english: Undiluted - That he dilutes it with water after having placed it into the cup undiluted; but to recite the blessing over it undiluted — didn't we say in the mishna that one does not recite a blessing? Alternatively: ḥai [means] in Old French fresche [fresh] — to bring it from the barrel for its sake.

Rashi on Berakhot 51a:19:1.hebrew: מעטרהו בתלמידים - תלמידיו סובבין אותו כשהוא מברך:
Rashi on Berakhot 51a:19:1.english: Adorns it with students - His students surround him when he recites the blessing.

Rashi on Berakhot 51a:19:3.hebrew: ובברכת הארץ - כשמגיע לברכת הארץ, מוסיף עליה:
Rashi on Berakhot 51a:19:3.english: And in the blessing of the land - When he reaches the blessing of the land, he adds [water] to it [the cup].

Rashi on Berakhot 51a:1:1.hebrew: במידי דלא ממאיס נמי - למה לי פולטן? לסלקינהו לצד אחד:
Rashi on Berakhot 51a:1:1.english: In [the case of] an item that does not become disgusting as well - Why must he spit them out? Let him move them to one side.

Rashi on Berakhot 51a:2:1.hebrew: מי שאכל ושתה ולא ברך - לפניהם קאי, אברכת המוציא וברכת היין:
Rashi on Berakhot 51a:2:1.english: One who ate and drank and did not recite a blessing - It refers to [the blessing recited] before them: to the blessing of HaMotzi and the blessing of wine.

Rashi on Berakhot 51a:2:2.hebrew: מהו שיחזור וכו' - לאחר אכילה ושתיה:
Rashi on Berakhot 51a:2:2.english: What is [the ruling: may] he return, etc. - [May he return and recite the blessing] after eating and drinking?

Rashi on Berakhot 51a:2:3.hebrew: יחזור ויאכל שום אחר - כדי שיסריח יותר? כלומר, יוסיף על סרחונו ויעשה ברכה לבטלה:
Rashi on Berakhot 51a:2:3.english: Should he return and eat another garlic - In order to stink more? That is to say, [shall he] add to his offense and recite a blessing in vain?

Rashi on Berakhot 51a:3:1.hebrew: הלכך - כיון דאם נזכר באמצע יכול לברך, אפי' גמר סעודתו נמי יכול לברך:
Rashi on Berakhot 51a:3:1.english: Therefore - Since if he remembered in the middle [of the meal] he can recite a blessing, even if he finished his meal, he can also recite [a blessing].

Rashi on Berakhot 51a:3:2.hebrew: על הטבילה - אלמא, אע"ג דטבל, הויא ברכה:
Rashi on Berakhot 51a:3:2.english: Concerning immersion - Evidently, even though he [already] immersed, it is a [valid] blessing.

Rashi on Berakhot 51a:4:1.hebrew: התם מעיקרא לא חזי - דרוב טבילות משום קרי הם, ובעלי קריין אסורים בברכות שהם דברי תורה, כדאמרינן בפרק מי שמתו (ברכות ד' כ:). ודחוי מעיקרא לאו דחוי הוא, ולכי מתקן הדר מברך. אבל האי מעיקרא איחזי, וכיון דגמ' אידחי, והואיל ואידחי — אידחי:
Rashi on Berakhot 51a:4:1.english: There, initially he was not fit - For most immersions are due to a seminal emission, and those who have experienced a seminal emission are forbidden from [reciting] blessings, which are words of Torah, as we say in the chapter [entitled] Mi SheMeto (Berakhot 20b). And an exclusion from the outset is not considered an exclusion, and once he rectifies [his status], he may then recite the blessing. However, this one was initially fit [to recite the blessing], and since he finished [his meal], he was excluded; and since he was excluded — he remains excluded.

Rashi on Berakhot 51a:5:1.hebrew: אספרגוס - כוס שהיו שותים בכל בקר אליבא ריקנא לרפואה:
Rashi on Berakhot 51a:5:1.english: Asparagus - A cup that they would drink every morning on an empty stomach for medicinal purposes.

Rashi on Berakhot 51a:6:1.hebrew: דבחמרא עסקינן - דאמרינן לקמן בשמעתין: אספרגוס ללע"ט יפה, ואוקמינן בשל יין. וסימן לע"ט: לב, עין, טחול:
Rashi on Berakhot 51a:6:1.english: That we are dealing with wine - For we say later in our sugya: "Asparagus is beneficial for L-E-T," and we establish it [as referring to asparagus made] of wine. And the mnemonic for L-E-T [is]: heart [lev], eye [ayin], spleen [teḥol].

Rashi on Berakhot 51a:6:2.hebrew: וכ״ש לבני מעים - קושיא היא. כלו', בדחמרא קתני וכ״ש לבני מעים:
Rashi on Berakhot 51a:6:2.english: And all the more so for the intestines - This is a difficulty. That is to say, [the baraita] teaches [concerning asparagus] in wine, and [yet it teaches] "and all the more so for the intestines."

Rashi on Berakhot 51a:6:3.hebrew: והתניא - לקמן, לרמ"ת קשה אספרגוס של יין. וסימן רמ"ת: ראש, מעים, תחתוניות:
Rashi on Berakhot 51a:6:3.english: And wasn't it taught - Later [in the sugya, it is established that] asparagus [made] of wine is harmful for *R-M-T*. And the mnemonic *R-M-T* [stands for]: *rosh* [head], *me'ayim* [intestines], [and] *taḥtoniyot* [hemorrhoids].

Rashi on Berakhot 51a:7:1.hebrew: כי תניא ההיא - דקתני: וכ"ש לבני מעים:
Rashi on Berakhot 51a:7:1.english: When that [baraita] was taught - [The baraita] that teaches: "And all the more so for the intestines."

Rashi on Berakhot 51a:7:2.hebrew: ביין מיושן - של ג' שנים, כדתנן בבבא בתרא (ד' צח.): ישן משל אשתקד, מיושן של שלש שנים:
Rashi on Berakhot 51a:7:2.english: With aged wine - [Wine] of three years, as we learned in the mishna in Bava Batra (98a): "Old [wine is] from last year; aged [wine is] of three years."

Rashi on Berakhot 51a:7:3.english: Konam is the wine that I taste - The wine that I taste shall be upon me like consecrated property.

Rashi on Berakhot 51a:8:1.hebrew: אלא חי - יין חי שאינו מזוג:
Rashi on Berakhot 51a:8:1.english: Only undiluted - Undiluted wine, which is not mixed [with water].

Rashi on Berakhot 51a:8:2.hebrew: אלא חי - יין חי שאינו מזוג:
Rashi on Berakhot 51a:8:2.english: Only undiluted - Raw wine that is not diluted [with water].

Rashi on Berakhot 51a:8:3.english: One does not pause while [drinking] it - Rather, one drinks it all at once.

Rashi on Berakhot 51a:8:4.english: And one does not follow it - To eat immediately after it.

Rashi on Berakhot 51a:9:1.english: In [the case of asparagus made] of wine - Its supplementation [is] with bread.

Rashi on Berakhot 51a:9:2.hebrew: בדשכרא - סמיכתו במינו — אם שכר תאנים, סומכו בתאנים; ואם של תמרים הוא, סומכו בתמרים:
Rashi on Berakhot 51a:9:2.english: [Asparagus made] of beer - Its supplementation is with its own kind: if [it is] fig beer, one supplements it with figs; and if it is [made] of dates, one supplements it with dates.

Tosafot on Berakhot 51a:17:1.hebrew: אין לנו אלא ארבעה דברים - ומיהו לא משמע (כן) דפליג ר' יוחנן אההיא דנותנו לימינו, כדאמרי' לקמן: א"ר יוחנן, ראשונים שאלו מהו שתסייע שמאל לימין — משמע שכן היו נוהגים. ומיהו, מדהאמוראים היו עושים עיטור ועיטוף, משמע שהיו מחמירים על עצמן והיו נזהרים בכולן; ולפיכך יש להחמיר בכוס של ברכה:
Tosafot on Berakhot 51a:17:1.english: "We have only four things" - However, it does not imply (so) that Rabbi Yoḥanan disagrees with that [teaching] of "he places it in his right [hand]," as we say below: "Rabbi Yoḥanan said: The early [Sages] asked: What is [the ruling as to whether] the left may assist the right?" — which implies that they were indeed accustomed to do so. Nevertheless, since the Amora'im would perform adorning and wrapping, it implies that they were stringent upon themselves and were careful regarding all of them; and therefore, one should be stringent regarding a cup of blessing.

Tosafot on Berakhot 51a:17:2.hebrew: שטיפה חי ומלא - ירושלמי דסוף פירקין: א"ר אחא, שלשה דברים נאמרו בכוס של ברכה: מלא, עיטור ומודח. ושלשתן מקרא: "נפתלי שבע רצון ומלא ברכת ה'". "שבע" — עיטור, "רצון" — מודח, "ומלא" — כמשמעו:
Tosafot on Berakhot 51a:17:2.english: Washing, undiluted, and full - The Yerushalmi at the end of our chapter [states]: Rabbi Aḥa said: Three things were said with regard to the cup of blessing: full, adorning, and rinsed. And all three of them [are derived from a single] verse: "Naphtali, satisfied with favor, and full of the blessing of the Lord" (Deuteronomy 33:23). "Satisfied" [refers to] adorning; "favor" [refers to being] rinsed; and "full" [is] according to its literal meaning.

Tosafot on Berakhot 51a:17:3.hebrew: שטיפה מבחוץ והדחה מבפנים - ופי' ר"י: דוקא שאין הכוס יפה, שיש בו שיורי כוסות; אבל אם הוא יפה בלאו הכי, שפיר דמי — דלא בעינן אלא שיהא כוס של ברכה יפה:
Tosafot on Berakhot 51a:17:3.english: "Washing from the outside and rinsing from the inside" - And the Ri explained that [this applies] specifically when the cup is not clean, in that it contains cup leftovers; but if it is clean without this, it is well, for we require only that the cup of blessing be clean.

Tosafot on Berakhot 51a:18:1.hebrew: זוכה לשני עולמות - פי' הרב רבי יוסף ממרשיליי"א: מדהוה ליה למכתב "ים ודרום רש" וכתב "ירשה", הרי יו"ד ה"א יתירה; וביו"ד ה"א נבראו שני עולמות, כדאמרינן בהתכלת (מנחות ד' כט:): "כי ביה ה' צור עולמים" (אל תקרי "צור" אלא "צר", וכו'):
Tosafot on Berakhot 51a:18:1.english: "He merits two worlds" - The Rabbi, Rabbi Yosef of Marseille, explained: Since [the verse] should have written "the sea and the south, possess" [yam vedarom resh], and it wrote "yerashah," behold, [the letters] yod [and] heh are extra; and with yod [and] heh the two worlds were created, as we say in [the chapter] HaTekhelet (Menachot 29b): "For in Yah the Lord is an eternal Rock" [Isaiah 26:4] (do not read "Rock" [tzur], but rather "He formed" [tzar], etc.).

Tosafot on Berakhot 51a:22:1.hebrew: שמאל מהו שתסייע לימין - בכוסות גדולות מיירי; או בראש חדש טבת שחל להיות בשבת — שהוא בחנוכה — או בנישואין, וצריך להאריך בברכת המזון:
Tosafot on Berakhot 51a:22:1.english: "What is the ruling: may the left assist the right?" - [This] is dealing with large cups; or with Rosh Chodesh Tevet that falls on Shabbat — which is during Hanukkah — or with a wedding, where one needs to prolong the Grace after Meals.

Tosafot on Berakhot 51a:4:1.hebrew: מעיקרא גברא לא חזי - תימה: והלא טמא אינו אסור לברך? ובקונטרס פירש דבעלי קריין אסורים בדברי תורה. וי"ל דמיירי בטבילת גרים, ומפני אותה טבילה הצריכו לכל שאר טבילות לברך לאחר טבילה. וכן בנט"י, שפעמים אדם בא מבית הכסא ואין אדם ראוי לברך עד לאחר הנטילה, נהגו העם לברך כל שאר ברכת ידים לאחר נטילה:
Tosafot on Berakhot 51a:4:1.english: "Initially, the person was not fit" - This is astonishing: Is a ritually impure person forbidden to recite a blessing? And in the Kuntres, [Rashi] explained that those who have had a seminal emission are forbidden from words of Torah. And one can say that [the baraita] deals with the immersion of converts, and on account of that immersion, they required for all other immersions to recite the blessing after immersion. And similarly regarding the washing of hands [netilat yadayim]: since sometimes a person comes from the bathroom and a person is not fit to recite a blessing until after the washing, people adopted the custom to recite all other blessings of the hands after washing.
